session_note: Retrieved by the Coordinator (this session) while resolving EXP-JMV-001's Control C1 blocker. specification.yaml's status_at_approval for C1 stated 'NOT SATISFIED. No agent in this program has read arXiv:math/0411378v3. The paper is not in the corpus.' This program's corpus DID already hold a different, related paper by the same three authors (David Jao, Stephen D. Miller, Ramarathnam Venkatesan) at inputs/ECTD-TESKE-20260731/sources/jmv-0811.0647.pdf ('Expander graphs based on GRH with an application to elliptic curve cryptography', arXiv:0811.0647v2) -- confirmed, by reading that PDF's own bibliography (reference [25]), to CITE arXiv:math/0411378 under its published title 'Do all elliptic curves of the same order have the same difficulty of discrete log?', Advances in Cryptology -- ASIACRYPT 2005, LNCS 3788, pp. 21-40. This is a different paper from 0811.0647, not a substitute for it. WebFetch against https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0411378 independently confirmed the title, authors, ASIACRYPT 2005 venue, and version history (v1 2004-11-17, v2 2005-08-31, v3 2005-09-02, current) before any bytes were retrieved. The PDF was then fetched directly and archived here so Control C1 (independent review of the held transcription against the actual source) becomes satisfiable, which it was not before this retrieval.

Authors: David Jao, Stephen D. Miller, Ramarathnam Venkatesan

attempts.purpose: Retrieve the full paper text and Figure 1 (the table under test by EXP-JMV-001) for Control C1/C1b review.
attempts.method: curl -sS -L (sandboxed session shell, through the environment's configured HTTPS proxy)
attempts.reason: Vendored verbatim (26-page PDF, sha256 pinned above) so this run's Control C1 review is reproducible without a second network fetch and so the object under test is frozen at the moment of retrieval, exactly as this program vendors other cited PDFs (see inputs/ECTD-TESKE-20260731/sources/*.pdf, inputs/BENNETT-WEAKNESS-2023/*.pdf).
figures_confirmed_in_retrieved_page: Fig. 1 (page 5 of the PDF): 16 rows -- NIST P-192/P-256/P-384/P-521 (4), NIST K-163/K-233/K-283/K-409/K-571 (5), NIST B-163/B-233/B-283/B-409/B-571 (5), IPSec 3rdOG F_2^155 and 4thOG F_2^185 (2). NO P-224 ROW EXISTS IN THE PUBLISHED FIGURE.

K-409: c_pi = 21262439877311*22431439539154506863*P(c_pi), P(c_pi) printed = 57030553306655053533734286593 9021184135396238924389891(contd) -- the string '(contd)' is printed verbatim in the published table; the value is genuinely truncated in the source itself, confirmed by direct visual inspection of the rendered PDF page (not just pdftotext extraction).
B-163, B-233, B-283, B-409, B-571, both IPSec rows: c_pi=1, P(c_pi)=1 for all.
Caption text: 'Note that the value of cpi for each of the standards curves is small (at most 3), except for the curves in the NIST K (Koblitz curve) family.'

Body text (Section 1, before Fig. 1): 'in Figure 1, we find that 10 out of the 11 randomly generated curves appearing in international standards documents have only one level' -- the 11 randomly-generated curves are the 4 P-rows + 5 B-rows + 2 IPSec rows (9+2=11); the 5 K-rows are explicitly non-random (deliberately selected for large c_pi) and excluded from that count.
attempts.note_on_rendering: pdftotext without -layout interleaves the c_pi and P(c_pi) columns confusingly for the multi-line K-row entries; pdftotext -layout (also archived, jmv-math-0411378v3-layout.txt) preserves the table columns correctly and was cross-checked against a direct visual render of PDF page 5 (via the Read tool's PDF page-image support) before any figure above was recorded here.
